questions.stem:
Whenever Sandra's mobile phone is flashing a blue light, it means that the battery is going to run out in five minutes.

Sandra: “The light is not flashing blue right now, so the battery will last a long time.”

Sam: “The blue light is on continuously – that must mean that the battery is going to run out in five minutes.”

If the information in the box is true, whose reasoning is correct?

steps.explain: The rule only tells us: flashing blue → battery runs out in 5 minutes.
Sandra: no flashing light does not tell us how long the battery will last. She has reversed the rule.
Sam: a light that is on continuously is not flashing, so the rule says nothing about it.

keyPoints.text: Whenever Sandra's mobile phone is flashing a blue light
keyPoints.note: The rule is only about a FLASHING blue light.
Continuous is not the same as flashing.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
Barking is a big deal. Of dog breeds, beagles are often cited as being the most vocal. They will alert you about anything that moves or comes by the door.
On the other hand, cavalier king Charles spaniels are one of the quietest dog breeds. Each of Emma's dogs is a cross between a beagle and a cavalier king Charles spaniel.

Emma: “All of my dogs are moderate barkers.”

If the information in the box is true, which of the following sentences shows the mistake Emma has made?
options: The mix of a great barker and quiet dog will result in a moderate barker.
Emma lives in an apartment so she must have a moderate, barking dog.
There is no information on barking of mixed dogs.

steps.explain: Emma assumes a cross between a loud breed and a quiet breed must be ‘in the middle’.
The box only describes beagles and cavalier king Charles spaniels. It says nothing about how much a cross-breed barks — it could be loud, quiet or moderate.
A just repeats Emma's assumption; B and C bring in things not in the box.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:

I plan to have a large cheese roll on Monday and Thursday, a chicken baguette with salad on Tuesday and a large egg roll on Wednesday and Friday.

The canteen has a special offer: if I order all of my sandwiches for the week then I will get the cheapest one free.

How much will I need to pay for my sandwiches for the week?

questions.stem:
If Stephanie does not sleep early, she will wake up late.
If she wakes up late, she will miss the bus.
If she does not miss the bus, she may get to school on time. If not, she will be late.

If the above statements are correct, which one of the following is not possible?
options: Stephanie slept early but wakes up late.
Stephanie catches the bus and is late to school.
Stephanie wakes up early and misses the bus.
Stephanie wakes up late but is not late for school.

steps.explain: Follow the chain for waking up late: wake up late → miss the bus → late for school.
So waking up late but NOT being late for school breaks the rules.

A is possible (the rules don't say what happens if she sleeps early). B is possible (catching the bus only means she MAY be on time). C is possible (the rules don't say waking early guarantees catching the bus).

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
Amy writes down the whole alphabet in order.

She then chooses a pair of letters, G and S. She finds the letter that is three quarters of the way between them.

Then she chooses another pair of letters. She finds that the letter half-way between these letters is the same as the letter she found three quarters of the way in the previous pair.

If the first letter of the second pair is K, what is the other letter?

steps.explain: Number the letters: G = 7 and S = 19. The gap is 12 letters.
Three quarters of the way from G is 9 letters after G.
P is half-way between K (11) and the other letter, which must be the same distance past P.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
Bert is auditioning for ‘The Talent Show’. The participants can perform any talent or skills they have. All contestants needed to fill out an online application form to be able to take part in the audition.

If a contestant could dance, they did not need to sing well. If they could not, then they either had to be able to play instruments decently or perform a magic show.

Bert is an experienced dancer but failed to pass the audition.

What must have been the reason?
options: He made a mistake in his magic show.
He did not know how to sing.
He did not dance to a difficult song.
He did not fill in the online form.

steps.explain: Bert can dance, so he did not need to sing well, play an instrument or do magic.
steps.work: B and A are not required for a dancer

steps.explain: Nothing says the song had to be difficult (C).
The one requirement left for everyone is the online application form. If Bert failed, that must be the reason.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:

Which of the following statements is true?

questions.stem:
One of the benefits of living in a house is that you get more space. Most houses have a separate garage where you can securely park your car and use the garage as a storage space. Also, houses offer backyards and front yards which you can use as your personal outdoor space.

If the information in the box is true, which of the following most weakens the argument?
options: Houses require many maintenance jobs, like plumbing and electrical issues.
Apartments often come with various amenities, like a swimming pool, gym or sauna facilities.
Living in apartments in the city can grant you a new lifestyle change which provides more comfort.
Apartments provide a gated door system so you feel more secure.

steps.explain: The argument says living in a house is better because it gives you more space — a garage and yards.
A weakener should show a downside of houses that the argument ignores.
A points out that houses come with many maintenance jobs (plumbing, electrical) — the extra space brings extra work and cost.
B, C and D praise apartments, but don't directly challenge the claimed benefit of a house.

questions.stem:
Just how critical are fire extinguishers for society in general? Fire extinguishers are extremely important as they are the most commonly used for fire protection. In many cases they are a first line of defence and often contain or extinguish a fire, preventing costly damage. These often overlooked devices can be a key component towards keeping you safe during a fire emergency situation. Business owners sometimes view fire extinguishers as red cans simply hanging on the wall, and an expense to managing their business. But these red cans serve a very useful purpose. It is essential to understand which extinguisher type should be used. Extinguishers with different coloured bands around them are used in different situations.

Mia: “So all fire extinguishers bottles are a red colour.”

Larry: “Fire extinguishers can save lives and prevent damage to property if you use them properly.”

If the information in the box is true, whose reasoning is correct?

steps.explain: Mia: the passage calls fire extinguishers ‘red cans’ and says ‘these red cans serve a very useful purpose’. Different types are told apart by the coloured BAND around them — the bottles themselves are red.
Larry: the passage says extinguishers contain or put out fires, prevent costly damage and keep you safe — as long as the right type is used.

questions.stem:
In a survey of school children, everyone who liked art liked sports.
Everyone who liked sports liked dancing, but no one who liked sports liked reading.

Based on the above information, which one of the following must be true?

If Sarah likes art, she does not like reading.
If Nicole does not like reading, she does not like dancing.
If Kevin does not like art, he does not like sport.

steps.explain: Write the rules as arrows.
steps.work: art → sports → dancing,   sports → NOT reading

steps.explain: Sarah likes art → she likes sports → she does not like reading.
A reverses an arrow (dancing does not have to mean sports). C and D also reason backwards from the rules.

Five students had a race to run across a soccer field to the goal post and back to see who runs the fastest.

No one arrived after Andrew.
Bruce arrived before Chris.
Two students were faster than Chris.
Sam was faster than Bruce.

Where did Joshua finish?

steps.explain: Andrew was last (5th). Two students were faster than Chris, so Chris was 3rd.
Bruce beat Chris and Sam beat Bruce, so Sam was 1st and Bruce 2nd.
The only place left for Joshua is 4th.

questions.stem:
Aviation contributes to about 2% of the world's global carbon emissions and climate change. Researchers predict passenger numbers will double by 2037.

Harry: “Since this is bad for everyone, airlines should be required to pay a tax on fuel. The money raised could be used to seek ways to deal with the problem of pollution. Airlines would pass on the cost by increasing airfares, thus passengers would be making a financial contribution to compensate for the damage they cause. This would be the fairest solution to the pollution problems caused by air travel.”

Which of the following, if true, most strengthens Harry's argument?
options: Fewer people would fly if airfares were increased.
World trade would suffer if aviation fuel were taxed.
Scientists think that the process of climate change cannot be reversed.
Air travel has increased because more people travel to holiday destinations.

steps.explain: Harry wants a fuel tax that raises airfares, to deal with pollution from flying.
A shows an extra benefit: higher fares mean fewer flights, so less pollution. This supports the tax.
B is a cost of the tax (weakens). C suggests nothing can help (weakens). D explains the growth in travel but doesn't support the tax.

B has no shower room in the main bedroom.
C has a separate toilet room, but the toilet should be in the bathroom.
In A the kitchen is reached from the hall, with a solid wall between it and the living room — the living room does not lead to the kitchen.
D matches every part of the description.

questions.stem:
Many shift workers experience sleep problems when they begin working irregular hours which makes it difficult for workers to have a routine of eating and drinking. Many people also experience a severe decline in their appetite, especially during the nightshift when they would normally be asleep.

Which one of these statements, if true, most strengthens the above argument?
options: People tend to dislike working shifts because they cannot schedule appointments with friends.
Night shift workers always lose weight in the first month of their roster.
Some people prefer working at night because shift work often pays better than working days only.
There is nowhere to buy food for night shift workers.

steps.explain: The argument: irregular shifts upset eating routines and reduce appetite.
B gives evidence of the effect — night shift workers lose weight when they start, which is what you'd expect if they eat less.
A is about social life, C is about pay. D gives a different reason for not eating (no food available), not loss of appetite.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
In a room there are four boxes and only one of the boxes has jewels in it. Each box has one statement written on it but only one of the four statements is true.

Peter has only one chance to choose the right box and finding the jewels using the clues given.

Box 1: “The jewels are here.”
Box 2: “The jewels are in the box 1 or 4.”
Box 3: “The jewels are not here.”
Box 4: “The jewels are here.”

Which box should Peter choose?

steps.explain: Try each box and count the true statements — exactly one must be true.
Jewels in Box 1: statements 1, 2 and 3 are true ✗.  Box 4: statements 2, 3 and 4 are true ✗.
Jewels in Box 3: all four statements are false ✗.
Jewels in Box 2: only statement 3 is true ✓

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
Kathy's school wanted to determine how playing different sports affected students' intelligence.

They made all the players take an IQ test. This is what they found:

• The best soccer players had a higher IQ than those who swim.
• All swimmers had a higher IQ than all those who play basketball.
• All basketball players had a higher IQ than most of those who play soccer.

Which of these sentences can be concluded from the above information?
options: Soccer players had the highest range of IQ.
Basketball players were generally good at playing soccer.
On average, the smartest people play soccer.
To be intelligent, it is better for a student to be able to swim and play basketball over playing soccer.

steps.explain: Order the groups: the best soccer players are above the swimmers, swimmers are above basketball players, and basketball players are above most soccer players.
steps.work: top soccer > swimmers > basketball > most soccer

steps.explain: So soccer players include both the highest IQs AND the lowest IQs — they have the widest spread (range).
C is wrong — most soccer players are at the bottom. B and D are not supported.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

Using the diagram above, which one of the following statements is correct?

options: PQ + RQ is equal to PR.
The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.

steps.explain: B is false: in any triangle, two sides together are longer than the third side, so PQ + RQ > PR.
We are only told PQ = PR. Nothing tells us where S is on PR, so we can't compare PS with SR (C).
Whether SQ is longer than PQ (A) depends on the angles and where S is, which we don't know.

questions.stem:
Among the 1000 people attending a cricket game, there were X number of students from school A and Y number of students who were not from school A.

Value 1: The number of people attending the game who were not students.
Value 2: 1000 – X – Y
Value 3: X + Y

Which of the following statements is correct?

steps.explain: Every student is either from school A or not from school A, so X + Y is the total number of students.
Everyone else is not a student.
So Value 1 and Value 2 are the same number. (We can't compare with Value 3 without numbers.)

questions.stem:
Sandra's mother has written to the school. She has suggested that, for the benefit of the children, the amount of vocabulary homework to be learnt each week should be reduced as she finds that it is too time consuming.

Which one of these statements, if true, most strengthens Sandra's mother's argument?
options: Good vocabulary skills will develop communication skills which helps students express themselves better.
Students need to do various outdoor activities to stay active and maintain their health.
The ability to vary the phrasing and using alternate terms can result in more interesting sentences or paragraphs in creative writing.
Vocabulary skills help improve reading comprehension.

steps.explain: Her argument: vocabulary homework takes too much time, so reduce it for the children's benefit.
A, C and D all give reasons why vocabulary is valuable — they weaken her argument.
B shows children need that time for something else important (being active and healthy), which supports cutting the homework.

questions.stem:
Space is quite literally anything and everything. It's one of the most challenging aspects of human learning. Astronauts are specially trained people to travel into outer space. They must be technically knowledgeable and be able to handle stressful situations that may arise during the mission. They have to be isolated from family and friends, and be exposed to radiation that could increase health risk for disease. Transitioning from one gravity field to another is trickier than it sounds. It affects your spatial orientation, head-eye and hand-eye coordination, balance, locomotion, and you're likely to experience motion sickness.

Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the above argument?
options: Space exploration allows new planets to be discovered, which can solve the problem of Earth's over population.
Researchers are looking into using virtual reality to simulate relaxing environments to help improve the mood of crews in isolation.
Travelling to space takes 6 to 12-month missions and years of training before that.
Ensuring astronauts get quality sleep is very important as there is no clear difference between day and night like we have on Earth.

steps.explain: The passage focuses only on how hard and risky space travel is — stress, isolation, radiation and gravity changes.
A gives a strong reason in favour of space travel: exploring space may find new planets and help solve Earth's overpopulation. This shows the difficulties may be worth it.
B only eases one small problem. C and D describe more difficulties, so they support the passage.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:

• Three of them went indoor climbing.
• Jason and Larry won a tennis tournament.
• Felicity and Peter learned to make origami birds.
• Felicity was tired after she went swimming.
• Jason and Larry were the only boys that went climbing.

Which person did the fewest activities?

steps.explain: Three went climbing, and the only boys who climbed were Jason and Larry — so the third climber is Felicity. Peter did not climb.
Count each person's activities.
steps.work: Jason: climbing, tennis = 2.  Larry: climbing, tennis = 2.  Felicity: climbing, origami, swimming = 3.  Peter: origami = 1.

questions.stem:
In Koscova, every day is either stormy or sunny. It is never stormy three days in a row and it is never sunny three days in a row. It's always stormy on Tuesday and Wednesday and it is always sunny on Saturday.

How many sunny days are there every week in Koscova?

steps.explain: Tuesday and Wednesday are stormy, so Monday and Thursday must be sunny (no three stormy days in a row).
Thursday and Saturday are sunny, so Friday must be stormy (no three sunny days in a row).
Saturday and next Monday are sunny, so Sunday must be stormy.
Sunny days: Monday, Thursday, Saturday.

questions.stem:
At Nancy's school, students who received an award in the athletics carnival can be nominated to be a House Captain.

Nancy: “I know that a total of fifteen awards were given in the athletics carnival this year. This means that fifteen of our students will be the candidates for House Captain!”

Which of the following sentences shows the mistake Nancy has made?
options: The number awards this year may be higher than usual.
There can not be fifteen house captains.
Some of the students from Nancy's school may have received multiple awards.
Some records may have been broken more than once.

steps.explain: Nancy assumes 15 awards means 15 different students.
If one student won two or more awards, there would be fewer than 15 award-winners — and fewer candidates.
(Also, award-winners CAN be nominated — it doesn't mean they all will be.) C points out her main mistake.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
“Whoever competes in a triathlon must be able to run, swim and cycle.”

If the information in the box is true, which one of these sentences must also be true?
options: If Aaron can run, he can swim too.
If Aaron does not run, he does not swim nor cycle.
If Aaron does not run, he cannot compete in a triathlon.
If Aaron can both run and swim, he can also cycle.

steps.explain: Rule: triathlon competitor → can run AND swim AND cycle.
If someone can't run, they can't meet the rule, so they can't compete.
A, B and D try to link running, swimming and cycling to each other — the rule says nothing about that.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
There is no better way to start the day than by blasting away unruly bed hair and the crust of sleep. For those who have a hard time waking up, a morning shower can make a big difference.

Dr Goldberg: “Humans tend to perspire at night. When you wake up in the morning, there's all this sweat and bacteria from the sheets that's just kind of sitting there on your skin.”

If the above passage is true, which of the following statement best weakens Dr Goldberg's argument?
options: Nighttime showering relieves stress brought on by a day of work and prepares the body for sleep.
Researchers shown that showering twice a day is more hygienic than once a day.
Very hot showers will strip your skin of its natural oils and irritate it more.
Sweat and gunk is produced overnight which needs to be washed off with a morning shower.

steps.explain: Dr Goldberg is arguing for a MORNING shower (to wash off the night's sweat).
A gives a good reason to shower at NIGHT instead, which weakens the case for the morning shower.
B is about showering twice, C is about hot water, and D supports Dr Goldberg.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

steps.explain: The box is a 3 × 1 × 1 block with a 1 × 1 × 1 cube on the middle. Its faces are: two T-shaped faces (front and back, 4 squares each), the bottom (3 squares), two ends, two ‘shoulder’ tops, two sides of the raised cube and its top — 18 squares in all.
D has only 17 squares, so it cannot work.
In each net the middle strip of 3 is the bottom, with a T-shaped face folding up on each side. Now check the extra squares at the ends of the strip.
In C, each end of the bottom folds up into: an end face → a shoulder top → a side of the raised cube, and the bottom chain carries on to the top of the raised cube. Every face appears exactly once.
A and B give some faces twice (e.g. two copies of the same shoulder) and leave the sides of the raised cube uncovered.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests
meta.note: Source net C did not fold correctly (one square misplaced); it was redrawn as a valid net. A, B and D are as in the source.

questions.stem:
Human activity affects plant and animal populations across local to global scales. Leading biologists, climate scientists and environmental watchdogs all agree – humanity's own impact on the environment is without a doubt the number one cause of species loss. People have always modified natural landscapes in the course of finding food, obtaining shelter and meeting other requirements of daily life.

If the information in the box is true, which of the following best weakens the argument?
options: Habitat destruction and modification are caused by humans.
Lower levels of human activity has resulted in a rise in animal population.
Animal populations are disturbed by human activity.
Some animal species prefer human companionship.

steps.explain: The argument: human impact is the main cause of species loss — humans are bad for animal populations.
A, B and C all support that idea (B shows animals do better with less human activity).
D is the only option suggesting humans can be good for some animals, which weakens the claim.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
In Slovandia, car number plates have two letters followed by two digits.

• The letters allowed are V, W, X and Y.
• The two letters must be different from each other.
• The digits allowed are 1, 2 and 3.
• The two digits can be the same but must not add up to 4 as this is considered unlucky.

How many different number plates could there be?

steps.explain: Letters: 4 choices for the first, 3 for the second (must be different).
Digits: 3 × 3 = 9 pairs, minus the ones adding to 4: 13, 31, 22.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
Shown below are the three small pieces of a puzzle.

Which one of the following big pieces can be combined with the three small pieces to make a square?

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 950 642" width="100%" height="auto" style="max-width:560px"><image href="/mts1/mts1-t2-q34.jpg" x="0" y="0" width="950" height="642"/></svg>

steps.explain: Each small piece has a sloping edge. In the finished square these slopes must line up with the sloping sides of the big piece, and the steps on top of each small piece must slot into the notches of the big piece.
Place the three small pieces around the big piece: one on each sloping side and one upside-down across the top, so that their outer edges form the four straight sides of the square.
Only in D do the notches and slopes match all three small pieces exactly, with no gaps or overlaps.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests
meta.note: Figure is the original book image (scanned).

questions.stem:
Susan: “My number is a two-digit number, less than 28 and it's even.”

John: “My number is also a two-digit number, divisible by 4 and 5.”

What is the biggest possible difference between Susan's number and John's number?

steps.explain: Susan's number is even, two-digit and less than 28: 10, 12, …, 26. The smallest is 10.
John's number is a multiple of 20 with two digits: 20, 40, 60 or 80. The largest is 80.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
A slow train departed from Central Station at 9:30 am and arrived at Newcastle at 1:00 pm. An express train departed from Central Station later and arrived at Newcastle at the same time as the slow train. The express train was three times as fast as the slow train. Each train travelled at a constant speed and did not stop along the way.

When did the express train depart from Central Station?

steps.explain: The slow train took 9:30 am to 1:00 pm.
Three times as fast means one third of the time.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
Whoever takes the photographs course must have both self-esteem and talent.

If the information in the box is true, which one of these sentences must also be true?
options: If Clare has both self-esteem and talent, she must have taken the photographs course.
If Clare did take the photographs course, she cannot have had self-esteem.
If Clare did not take the photographs course, she cannot have had talent.
If Clare did not have self-esteem, she cannot have taken the photographs course.

steps.explain: Rule: photographs course → self-esteem AND talent.
If Clare has no self-esteem, she doesn't meet the rule, so she cannot have taken the course.
A reverses the rule. B contradicts it. C draws a conclusion the rule doesn't support.

questions.stem:
To qualify for the MVP of the National Basketball Association, the player must meet at least one of three conditions:

1. Score a minimum of 50 points in the current season
2. Receive more than 10 votes by the panel
3. Must be from the winning team

Billy: “Jason's team won this year's tournament and he scored 60 points. He must become the MVP for this season.”

Joe: “Packer has scored 70 points this season, received 12 votes from the panel and his team won the final game. Packer will surely get the MVP.”

If the information in the box is true, whose reasoning is correct?

steps.explain: The conditions only decide who QUALIFIES for the MVP — they don't say who will win it.
Jason and Packer both qualify, but many players could qualify. Neither is sure to become MVP.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
The Saturday Telegraph – in conjunction with Sydney Metro – is offering readers the once-in-lifetime opportunity to walk through the completed harbour tunnel with 30 double passes on offer.

Joe: “You can walk through the harbour tunnels on Saturday.”

Clark: “30 people can walk through the harbour tunnel.”

If the information in the box is true, whose reasoning is correct?

steps.explain: ‘The Saturday Telegraph’ is the name of the newspaper — the box doesn't say the walk is on Saturday.
30 DOUBLE passes admit 2 people each, so 60 people can walk through.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
Online payments refer to the electronic exchange of currency through the internet. These payments usually consist of the transfer of monetary funds from a customer's bank or debit or credit card account, into the seller's bank account, in exchange for products or services. These funds can come directly from a customer's credit card or checking account, or from an online payment system that is linked to both the buyer and seller's bank accounts. Online payments are becoming increasingly popular because they are convenient and payments are instant.

If the above passage is true, which of the following statement best weakens the argument?
options: Online payments provide both the buyer and seller efficiency, convenience and contactless options.
If someone uses your electronic money it can be difficult to resolve the issue or get refunded.
Online payment is a more convenient and faster option compared to cash.
Technology continues to develop in e-commerce, and people are relying on the convenience of paying online.

steps.explain: The argument: online payments are popular because they are convenient and instant.
A, C and D all repeat or support the benefits of online payments.
B gives a real drawback — misuse is hard to fix or refund — a reason people might avoid online payments.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
The following shape is made from a square by cutting some pieces out.

Which of the following is the result when the above shape is rotated 270 degrees anticlockwise?

steps.explain: Turning 270° anticlockwise is the same as turning 90° (a quarter turn) clockwise.
In a quarter turn clockwise: the top edge moves to the right, the right edge moves to the bottom, the bottom edge moves to the left and the left edge moves to the top.
So the slot that opens to the RIGHT now opens DOWNWARD (at the bottom right), the gap at the bottom now opens to the LEFT, and the cut-away top-left corner moves to the top RIGHT.
A is a mirror image, B is a quarter turn anticlockwise, C is a half turn. D is the quarter turn clockwise.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests
meta.note: Options redrawn as exact transformations of the shape (mirror, 90° anticlockwise, 180°, 90° clockwise).

questions.stem:
SUVs (Sports Utility Vehicles) are known for being some of the most powerful passenger vehicles on the road today. These cars are larger than most others and it is also easier to see the rest of the road from the driver's seat. An SUV fills the void between a car and truck, giving the luxury of a sedan with the power and utility of a truck.

Which of these statements, if true, most weakens the argument?
options: Because of their height, SUVs have great visibility on the road.
Because of its increasing popularity SUVs have great resale value.
Sedans have lower weights and smaller engines, making them more economically efficient.
SUVs are great for camping or road trips because they have extra features like 4 x 4 capabilities which makes towing a trailer or boat simple.

steps.explain: The passage praises SUVs: powerful, large, good visibility, luxury plus utility.
A, B and D all add more good points about SUVs — they strengthen it.
C gives a reason a smaller car may be the better choice (cheaper to run), which weakens the case for SUVs.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
After lengthy periods of rain, some road pavements become saturated. The water in the pavement is compressed under the weight of traffic and this compressed water pops out any weak point in the asphalt forming a pothole.

Sophia: “If the asphalt already has some cracks, the roads get more potholes.”
James: “Dry days don't have as many potholes as wet days.”

If the information in the box is true, whose reasoning is correct?

steps.explain: The box says water bursts out through any WEAK POINT in the asphalt. Cracks are weak points, so cracked roads get more potholes.
Potholes form after LENGTHY periods of rain, and once formed they stay there on dry days too. The box doesn't compare the number of potholes on single dry and wet days.

questions.stem:
Samantha wants to make as many cupcakes as possible from the ingredients she has at home.
The recipe to make 4 cupcakes needs 50 g of flour, 50 g of sugar, 50 g of butter and 1 egg.

At home, she has 300 g of flour, 500 g of sugar, 300 g of butter and 5 eggs.

What is the maximum number of cupcakes Samantha can make?

steps.explain: Work out how many batches (of 4 cupcakes) each ingredient allows.
The eggs run out first, so she can make only 5 batches.

questions.stem:
Every year, Nancy's high school holds a musical performance night for the end of year celebration. The school is selecting players to perform and multiple instrument players are preferred but not essential. The school is selecting 40 people to perform at the concert.

Sam: “I have performed every year since year 7 so I definitely can perform this year too.”

Jonathan: “I only play one instrument, so I have a small chance of being selected to perform.”

If the information in the box is true, whose reasoning is correct?

steps.explain: Performing in past years doesn't guarantee being selected this year.
Playing several instruments is preferred but NOT essential, and we don't know how many people apply. Jonathan can't conclude his chance is small.

questions.stem:
A group of 50 instrument players were asked whether they play flute and/or play bugle.

40 people said that they play the flute and 20 said that they play the bugle.

If the above information is true, which one of these statements cannot be true?
options: Every student plays at least either the flute or the bugle.
At least 10 students play both the flute and bugle.
At least twice as many students play only the piano as the bugle.
At most 20 students play both the flute and the bugle.

steps.explain: 40 + 20 = 60, but there are only 50 players, so at least 10 play both. At most 20 play both (everyone who plays the bugle).
If exactly 10 play both, then 40 + 20 − 10 = 50 play at least one — everyone. So A could be true.
At least 40 players play the flute or the bugle, so at most 10 play neither (e.g. only the piano). Twice the bugle players would be 40 — impossible.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests
meta.note: Book key says A, but A is possible (exactly 10 play both → all 50 play one); C is the statement that cannot be true.

questions.stem:
Mr Clark set a test for his students last week which was made up of three parts.

Each of the three parts had 10 questions.

Questions in Part 1 were worth 2 marks each, those in Part 2 were worth 3 marks each and those in Part 3 were worth 5 marks each.

Mr Clark has set the pass mark to 70 out of 100.

What is the largest number of questions that could be correctly answered while failing the test?

steps.explain: To get many questions right but few marks, answer the cheapest questions first.
steps.work: All of Part 1: 10 × 2 = 20.  All of Part 2: 10 × 3 = 30.  Total 50 marks, 20 questions.

steps.explain: Failing means 69 marks or fewer, so there are 19 marks left for 5-mark questions.
A 24th question (5 marks) would make 70 — a pass.

questions.stem:
Jenny is planning a party next month. She invited all her friends and family to the party, expecting just 25 of them to be able to attend. She calculated that she needed to spend $8 on food and drink for each of the guests and ordered enough to cater for up to 35 guests.

When she had received all of the replies, she found that 40 of the people she had invited were going to attend.

She decided to provide less food and drink, spending a different amount per guest on food and drink.

How much did Jenny need to spend per person for 40 people in order to still spend the same budget as she originally planned?
questions.hint: Her budget was set by how many guests she ordered for, not how many she expected.

steps.explain: She ordered enough for 35 guests at $8 each — that is her budget.
Share the same budget between 40 guests.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
How much skin do you think it takes to cover the sole of your foot?
Trace the outline of your foot onto a piece of graph paper and count the number of squares to determine the area of the sole of your foot.
How much skin do you think it takes to cover your entire body?
There is a simple rule of thumb that can be used to find the area of your entire body.
If you multiply the area of your sole by one hundred, the answer will be the approximate area of your entire body.

Andrew's entire body area came out as 0.8 square metres.

What could be the area of his foot in square centimetres? Remember \(1\text{ m}^2 = 10\,000\text{ cm}^2\).

steps.explain: Change the body area to square centimetres.
The body is 100 times the sole, so divide by 100.

questions.stem:
The price for passes of a theme park are shown in the table below.

Pass for 1 day: $28 · Pass for 4 consecutive days: $50 · Pass for 7 consecutive days: $75

I will need a pass on the following days of the month: 1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 11, 12, 14, 15, 16.

How much is the cheapest valid combination I could use?

steps.explain: Days 10 to 16 fit in one 7-day pass.
Days 1, 2, 3, 5 span 5 days. A 4-day pass + a 1-day pass = $78, but one 7-day pass (days 1–7) = $75.
A single 4-day pass can't cover both 1 and 5, so $50 + $75 = $125 is impossible.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests
meta.note: Book key says C ($153), but two 7-day passes (days 1–7 and 10–16) cost $150, which is cheaper.

questions.stem:
I have a basket containing three types of fruits.

All but four are oranges, all but four are apples and all but four are bananas.

How many pieces of fruit are in the basket?

steps.explain: ‘All but four are oranges’ means apples + bananas = 4. Similarly oranges + bananas = 4 and oranges + apples = 4.
All three pairs add to 4, so each type has the same number: 2.

questions.stem:
If you are late to school, you must bring a note from your parent or guardian explaining the reason for being late. If you can't bring the note, you must go to the office and get a permission note to go into the classroom.

Sally and Megan were late to school and met at the school gate.

Sally: “I am late but I have my parent's note saying we had a broken car this morning. I can go into the classroom without any problem.”

Megan: “I couldn't get a note from my parents because they already left for work so I can't go into the classroom.”

If the information in the box is true, whose reasoning is correct?

steps.explain: Sally has the parent's note that the rule asks for, so she can go to class.
Megan has no note, but the rule says she can get a permission note from the office and then go into class.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
There are three grocery stores in town.
Twenty Seven opens every day from 10 am till 6 pm. It has the most fresh vegetables and fruits around. It has no parking space available.

Whole Mall opens Monday to Friday from 6 am until 12 noon. It has the biggest variety of groceries but is the most expensive.

Aldo opens Monday to Saturday 10 am to 6 pm, and is closed on Sunday.

Mrs Tang is a career woman who works Monday to Friday, arriving home at 6 pm. She normally drives to the grocery store.
She is planning to host a party on Sunday evening and wants to prepare enough food for 15 people.

Where should Mrs Tang do the shopping?
options: She will have to go to a grocery store out of town

steps.explain: Mrs Tang can only shop on Saturday or Sunday (she works until 6 pm on weekdays), and she drives.
Whole Mall is only open on weekdays until noon ✗. Twenty Seven is open at the weekend, but has no parking ✗.
Aldo is open on Saturday from 10 am to 6 pm, which suits her.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests
meta.note: Source said Whole Mall opens '6 am to 12 am'; clarified to 12 noon, the reading the intended answer depends on.

questions.stem:
Joanne believes that many teens are less likely to engage in activities like the older generations did, such as going to see friends and outdoor activities. Modern teens are learning to do most of their communication while looking at a screen, not another person. Spending too long on social media is associated with higher levels of mental problems, including anxiety, depression and psychological distress.

Which one of these statements, if true, most strengthens Joanne's argument?
options: Not all teens have access to tablets and computers.
Internet usage should be limited to children.
Mental health can be improved with more social interaction.
Social media helps make more friends for shy people.

steps.explain: Joanne: teens now spend less time with people face to face and more on screens, which is linked to mental health problems.
C supports the link: real social interaction improves mental health, so losing it is harmful.
A and D weaken her argument; B is a suggestion, not evidence.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
When Jessica's car is unlocked when parked, her phone will receive an alert. Otherwise, nothing happens to the phone.

Jessica: “I received an alert on my phone and went to lock the car. But I'm still getting the alert on my phone, so that means the car has not registered that it is locked.”

Whitney: “No, that's not right. The alert on the phone means that the car is still unlocked.”

If the information in the box is true, whose reasoning is correct?

steps.explain: The box says the phone gets an alert ONLY when the car is unlocked; otherwise nothing happens.
So if the alert keeps coming, the car really is still unlocked. Whitney is right.
Jessica blames the car for not ‘registering’ that it is locked — but by the rule, an alert means the car is unlocked, so her locking didn't work. Her explanation doesn't follow from the box.

questions.stem:
Eating chocolate for breakfast is not a bad idea at all. Chocolate is a treat which many people love. Many young people struggle to get out of bed in the morning and so the thought of a delicious chocolate bar could be enough to tempt them from their beds and therefore get to school on time.

Which one of the following statements, if true, most weakens the above argument?
options: Having more than the recommended daily intakes of chocolate can cause obesity in children.
Eating chocolate causes people to be sleepy in the middle of the day.
Young children cannot wake up without the temptation of food.
Chocolate is too expensive in large quantities.

steps.explain: The argument: chocolate for breakfast helps young people get up and get to school.
B shows chocolate makes people sleepy later in the day — so it would hurt their school day, the very thing the argument claims to help.
A is only about eating too much. C supports the argument. D is about cost, not the effect.

Tryouts for the school's baseball team happen every year. Each player needs to pass the tryouts to get into the team.

Darren: “I passed the tryouts and am currently in the school's baseball team. This means I will definitely be on the team next year.”

Which one of the following sentences shows the mistake Darren has made?
options: If Darren was good enough to pass this year, he will be good enough to pass next year.
The school's baseball team has a limited number of spots.
Darren had a fight with one of teammates this year.
There will be another tryouts next year.

steps.explain: Tryouts happen every year and every player must pass them.
So Darren must pass the tryouts AGAIN next year — passing this year doesn't guarantee a place next year.

questions.stem:
Some scientists were measuring the heights of different trees in a local forest. This was what was found:

• The shortest tree was a spruce tree.
• The tallest tree was an oak tree.
• Pine trees range from three to five metres tall.

Which one of these sentences can be concluded from the above information?
options: All oak trees are taller than all spruce trees.
At least one oak tree is more than five metres tall.
All spruce trees are shorter than all oak trees.
The shortest tree is four metres tall.

steps.explain: The tallest tree is an oak, and some pine trees are 5 m tall. So the tallest tree (an oak) must be taller than 5 m.
We only know about the single tallest and single shortest trees — not all oaks or all spruces (A, C).
The shortest tree is shorter than every pine, so it is less than 3 m, not 4 m (D).

questions.stem:
A word is made into a code using the following rule.
The first letter remains the same.
The second letter is changed to the letter that is one letter before that.
The third letter is changed to the letter that is two letters before that, and so on.

For example, SOLEMN is changed to SNJBII.

In the same code, what is represented by JNWLQN?

steps.explain: To decode, move each letter FORWARD: 1st by 0, 2nd by 1, 3rd by 2, and so on.

questions.stem:
Sandy got coffee orders for her café.

She knew that 5 people wanted coffee: 3 with milk, 2 with sugar.

Unfortunately, she did not know how many wanted both milk and sugar.

Which of the following would enable her to make the right 5 drinks, even if she could not work out which was for whom?
options: James takes just sugar and Ken takes neither.
Ken takes neither and Malcolm takes just milk.
Betty takes both and Ken takes neither.
Malcolm takes just milk and James takes just sugar.

steps.explain: Let b be the number who take both. Then: just milk = 3 − b, just sugar = 2 − b, neither = b (to make 5 people).
Someone takes NEITHER → b ≥ 1. Someone takes JUST SUGAR → 2 − b ≥ 1, so b ≤ 1.
A gives both facts, so b = 1: 1 both, 2 just milk, 1 just sugar, 1 neither. B, C and D each leave two possibilities.

steps.explain: Look for the chart whose bar heights follow the table.
Key features: March (314) and September (305) are by far the highest — almost 3 times most months; February (38) and August (42) are the lowest; the other months are all between 104 and 178.
Only D has two very tall bars at March and September and very short bars at February and August.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
If Julie doesn't study for her English test, she is likely to fail.

If she fails the test, she will not be given a chance to represent in the debating team for her school.

If she represents her school in debating, then she might get the end of year award. Otherwise she doesn't stand a chance.

If the above statements are true, which one of the following is not possible?
options: Julie did not study but passed English.
Julie did study but did not pass English.
Julie represented her school in debating but didn't get the end of year award.
Julie didn't pass in English but represented her school in debating.

steps.explain: A is possible: not studying only makes failing LIKELY. B is possible: the rules don't say studying guarantees a pass. C is possible: debating means she MIGHT get the award.
D breaks a rule: failing the test means she can't represent the school in debating.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

Andy's weight is two thirds of Ben's.

If 75% of Ben's weight is 36 kg, then who is the lightest of the four people?

steps.explain: 75% of Ben's weight is 36 kg.
Andy is two thirds of Ben.
Malcolm and Jason are each the average of two others.

questions.stem:
Jason, Charlie, Sylvia, Nick and Peter play hopscotch on a grid with the numbers 1-10.
Only Jason and Charlie throw their stones onto even numbers.
Nick's stone lands on a lower number than anyone else's.
Sylvia's stone lands on 7.
No two people throw their stone on to the same number.
Nobody's stone lands on the numbers 1, 5 or 10.
Peter's stone lands on an odd number higher than both Jason and Charlie.

If these statements are true, which one of the sentences below must be true?
options: Sylvia's stone lands on a higher number than Charlie's.

steps.explain: Nick and Peter land on odd numbers. The odd numbers allowed are 3, 7 and 9, and Sylvia has 7.
Nick has the lowest number, so Nick = 3 and Peter = 9.
Jason and Charlie are on even numbers above 3: two of 4, 6, 8 — so C is not certain (Charlie could be 8). A and D are impossible.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
My brother's aunt is Kelly.
Her husband is Sam.
Their son is Andrew.
He has one sister, Claris.

Which statement is correct?

steps.explain: My brother's aunt is also my aunt, so Kelly is my aunt, and her children Andrew and Claris are my cousins.
A is not certain — I may have other cousins (Andrew is one!). B and C are wrong — Claris is a cousin, not a niece.
Claris is the daughter of my parents' sister (or sister-in-law), so she is my father's niece.

questions.stem:
The beef and dairy cattle industry is one of the main contributors to global greenhouse gases. Methane makes up about half of the total greenhouse gases on earth. Cows generate methane in two main ways: through their digestion and through their waste.

Tom: “Methane gas emissions from livestock are a huge problem to the environment.”

Peter: “If more people become vegans, it would have a positive impact on the environment.”

If the information in the box is true, whose reasoning is correct?

steps.explain: The box says cattle are one of the main sources of greenhouse gases, mostly through methane.
Tom: methane from livestock is a big environmental problem — this matches the box.
Peter: vegans eat no meat, dairy or eggs. More vegans means fewer cattle are raised, so less methane — good for the environment.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
All year 6 students from Heights Primary School went to Lune Park for their mid-year excursion. There were three rides that were most popular among the students.
The rides were: Tango Train, Hair Raiser and Moon Ranger.

• Most children who rode Tango Train also rode Moon Ranger.
• All children who rode Tango Train also rode Hair Raiser.
• Some students who rode Moon Ranger also rode Hair Raiser.

We know that Joseph rode Hair Raiser. Which one of the following statements must be true?
options: Joseph rode Tango Train, but did not ride Moon Ranger.
Joseph rode Moon Ranger, but did not ride Tango Train.
Joseph rode both Tango Train and Moon Ranger.
There is not enough information to confirm whether Joseph rode either Tango Train or Moon Ranger.

steps.explain: The rules only go one way: Tango Train → Hair Raiser. Riding Hair Raiser does NOT mean you rode Tango Train.
Some Moon Ranger riders also rode Hair Raiser — but that doesn't mean every Hair Raiser rider rode Moon Ranger.
So knowing Joseph rode Hair Raiser tells us nothing certain about the other two rides.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
Elise broke her necklace.

She found one quarter of the beads on the carpet, one third down the side of the stool, one fifth in her bag, while one sixth remained in her hand; five beads were never found.

How many beads were there to start with?

steps.explain: Add up the fractions that were found (use 60ths).
The part never found:
\(\frac{1}{20}\) of the beads is 5 beads.

questions.stem:
Every year there are nearly 25 000 car fires, but not all drivers travel with a fire extinguisher in their car. Sam thinks that if more drivers could be encouraged to carry fire extinguishers then the number of car fires could be considerably reduced.

Which one of these statements, if true, most weakens Sam's argument?
options: Research shows that fire extinguishers are very effective in most car fires.
Most drivers never experience a car fire.
There is a possibility that the car fires cannot be put out with an extinguisher.
Whether a car is carrying an extinguisher or not does not affect the possibility of a car fire.

steps.explain: Sam claims carrying extinguishers would REDUCE THE NUMBER of car fires.
An extinguisher can put a fire out once it starts, but it can't stop a fire from starting.
D says exactly that — carrying an extinguisher doesn't change whether a fire happens — so the number of fires would not drop.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
Vitamin E is an essential nutrient for the body. It can be used externally on skin and hair. It fights free radicals and protects skin from oxidative damages.
It is reported that although Vitamin E, present in fresh fruits and vegetables is beneficial for the human body, capsule Vitamin E does not have the same effect.

If the information in the box is true, which of these statements most strengthens the argument?
options: Vitamin E is crucial to the health of animals.
Vitamin E in capsules allows healthier hair to grow.
Only Vitamin E in fruits is absorbed entirely by the small intestine.
The sale of capsule Vitamin E should be banned.

steps.explain: The argument: Vitamin E from fruit and vegetables helps the body, but capsules don't work as well.
C gives a reason why: only the Vitamin E in fruit is fully absorbed. That explains and supports the claim.
A is about animals. B praises capsules (weakens). D is an opinion, not evidence.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
Andy, Bobby and Harvey are playing with coins. They take turns to toss the coin on the table.

• If the coin shows heads, then that player must receive $1 from each of the two other players.
• If the coin shows tails, then that player must give $1 to each of the other two players.

Andy's and Bobby's coins show heads and Harvey's coin shows tails.

If Andy started with $10, how much does he have now?

steps.explain: Andy's heads: he gets $1 from each of the other two.
Bobby's heads: Andy pays Bobby $1.
Harvey's tails: Harvey gives Andy $1.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
It's normal for children to be fussy eaters. But food allergy is an immune system reaction that occurs soon after eating a certain food. Even tiny amounts of the allergy-causing food can trigger signs and symptoms. Anaphylaxis is a severe allergic reaction that needs urgent medical attention.

Which of the following best weakens the above argument?
options: Fussy eating is a natural part of children's development.
Some people like sweet food which can cause cavities and tooth decay.
The most common foods that cause allergic reactions are nuts, milk and shellfish.
People do not eat certain foods due to allergies that can harm them.

steps.explain: The passage separates fussy eating (‘normal’) from food allergies.
D suggests that some children who refuse foods may not be fussy at all — they may be avoiding foods that harm them. That challenges the idea that refusing food is just ‘normal’ fussiness.
A agrees with the passage; B and C don't affect the argument.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
Jenny lives in Liverpool. On Sunday she plans to visit her friend Sandra who lives in Mascot for lunch.

Her journey will consist of a 10-minute walk to Liverpool station, then a train ride to Mascot station and finally a bus ride to Sandra's house.

Trains leave Liverpool at 06:45 and then every 30 minutes until 21:15, taking 1 hour 20 minutes to reach Mascot.

Buses leave Mascot station at 08:00 and then every 20 minutes until 21:00, arriving at Sandra's house 12 minutes later.

Jenny left her house at 10:00 am.

What is the earliest time she can arrive at Sandra's house for lunch?

steps.explain: She reaches Liverpool station at 10:10. Trains leave at :15 and :45 past each hour, so she catches the 10:15.
Buses leave Mascot at :00, :20 and :40. The next one after 11:35 is 11:40.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
I saw 9 cars with bicycles on the roof in the parking lot.

Some of the cars were carrying one bicycle, and some had two.
Counting the wheels of the cars and the bicycles, there was a total of 60 wheels.

How many cars had 2 bicycles on the roof?

steps.explain: Car wheels:
Bicycle wheels and number of bicycles:
Each car has at least 1 bicycle (9); the extra 3 bicycles are second bikes.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
Hypochondriacs are people with illness anxiety disorder. They have an unrealistic fear that they have a serious medical condition or fear that they are at high risk of becoming ill. They misinterpret typical body functions as signs of illness. Even after medical tests show no problems, people with hypochondriasis are still preoccupied with the idea that they are seriously sick. It is important to treat hypochondriacs in the early stages.

If the information in the box is true, which of the following most strengthens the above argument?
options: Hypochondriacs don't trust doctors that they are taking their illness seriously.
Hypochondriasis typically appears during early adulthood but can affect all ages and genders.
Hypochondriacs can develop depression, anxiety or other mood changes.

steps.explain: The conclusion is that hypochondriacs should be treated EARLY.
D shows what can happen if it isn't treated — it can lead to depression, anxiety and other problems. That is a reason to treat it early.
B weakens it (rare = less urgent). A and C give facts but no reason for early treatment.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
Victor is planning a trip to Movie World and is calculating his budget.
He wants to go on the following rides:

Superman Escape*, DC Rivals⁺, Wild Wild West, Scooby-Doo*, Looney Tunes, Ghost Train⁺, Double Dragon of Fire*, Barrels of Fun*, Power Surge and Hair Raise.

Pricing: 1 ride costs $10 (* rides cost an extra $5, ⁺ rides cost an extra $10). A Day Pass costs $85, or $110 for rides including * or ⁺.

How much would Victor save by buying the Day Pass instead of buying individual tickets?

steps.explain: Individual tickets: 4 plain rides at $10, 4 * rides at $15 and 2 ⁺ rides at $20.
His rides include * and ⁺ rides, so he needs the $110 Day Pass.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
Laughter establishes or restores a positive emotional climate and a sense of connection between two people. In fact, some researchers believe that the major function of laughter is to bring people together – the more social a person is and the more social support a person receives, the more likely that laughter will result from that social connection.

If the information in the box is true, which one of the following most strengthens the above argument?
options: Laughing reduces pain and allows a higher toleration of discomfort.
People should not laugh too loudly in public places.
People who laugh a lot can overcome relationship problems more quickly.
When you laugh a lot, your heart rate increases rapidly.

steps.explain: The passage says laughter's main job is to connect people.
C shows laughter helping relationships — a social benefit, which supports the argument.
A and D are physical effects, and B is an opinion about manners.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
Life on Earth relies on energy – such as light and heat – from the sun. In fact, energy from the sun, called solar energy, is the most abundant energy resource on Earth.

You can feel the sun's energy as heat and see it as light. But how do we harness that energy to cook dinner or charge a phone? Solar panels!

You may have seen solar panels on the roof of a house or other buildings. These solar panels capture light energy from the sun and convert it into electricity that can be used by the people inside the building. Some power companies use solar panels as a source of electricity, too.

Clouds can block light from the sun, but depending on the types of clouds and where those clouds are, certain cloudy conditions can be great for the production of solar energy.

Sam: “Today is a cloudy day so our solar panel won't produce enough solar energy!”

Bexley: “We have solar panels on our roof. We can save a lot on electricity bills.”

If the information in the box is true, whose reasoning is correct?

steps.explain: The box says some cloudy conditions can be great for solar energy, so a cloudy day doesn't mean too little energy.
Solar panels make electricity for the people in the building, so they need less electricity from the power company — lower bills.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
Three friends, Sam, Alex and Harry have pencil cases with a different number of pens in each.

Sam: “Harry's pencil case has 5 pens less than Alex's pencil case.”
Alex: “Sam's pencil case has 3 more pens than the Harry's pencil case.”

If the information in the box is true, whose pencil case has the most number of pens?

steps.explain: Compare everyone with Harry: Alex has Harry + 5 and Sam has Harry + 3.
For example, if Harry has 10 pens, Alex has 15 and Sam has 13.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
Liam, Mary and Ben have 30 $1 coins each.

They take turns to roll a dice.

• If the number rolled is 1, 2 or 3, then that player gives the number of coins shown on the dice to each of the other two players.
• If the number rolled is 4, 5 or 6, then that player receives the number of coins shown on the dice from each of the other two players.

Liam rolls a 1.

Mary rolls a 3.

If the friends end up with $27, $21 and $42 respectively, which number did Ben roll?

steps.explain: Liam rolls 1: he gives $1 to each.
Mary rolls 3: she gives $3 to each.
Ben ends with $42, so he gained $8 — $4 from each of the others. Check: Liam 31 − 4 = 27 ✓, Mary 25 − 4 = 21 ✓.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
To get into a Sports High School, a student must be a member of the talented sport program they are seeking to represent. In a Sports High School, all students benefit from access to state-of-the-art onsite facilities and programs. All Sports High Schools offer a talented program in football.

To gain entry, students need to complete an application form and then attend a number of selection trials.

Eva: “I've been playing tennis since 5 years old so I should be able to get into a Sports High School.”

If the information in the box is true, which of the following shows the mistake Eva has made?
options: Eva is a member of the talented tennis program.
People who are only good at tennis will not be accepted to the Sport High School.
All talents sports people like to train in venues with state-of-the-art facilities.
All students must first attend the selection trials in order to be selected.

steps.explain: Eva thinks years of playing tennis are enough to get in.
But every student must apply AND go through selection trials — experience alone doesn't guarantee entry.
A and C don't show a mistake, and B is not stated in the box.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
Asbestos is the name used for a group of natural occurring minerals. They have resistance to high temperatures, fire, electricity and corrosion. These qualities make effective insulators, so they were popular in building products before the 1980s. They can also be added to cloth, paper, cement, plastic and other materials to make them stronger.

Kirk: “When asbestos dust is inhaled or ingested, the fibres can become permanently trapped in the body and cause inflammation, scarring and eventually genetic damage.”

If the information in the box is true, which of the following statements most strengthens Kirk's argument?
options: Exposure to asbestos can cause cancer and other health conditions.
Asbestos related diseases have a long latency period, often taking decades to develop.
Small amounts of asbestos may be allowed in some consumer products.
Extra protective gear needs to be worn when demolishing buildings comprising of asbestos.

steps.explain: Kirk's point is about asbestos DUST being breathed in or swallowed and harming the body.
D connects to this directly: when old asbestos buildings are knocked down, dust fills the air, so workers must wear masks and protective gear to avoid breathing it in.
C weakens the worry. A and B talk about disease in general rather than the dust being inhaled.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
Five people are standing in the same row during the school assembly. Each person owns a different pet and they all have different types of hobbies. We also know that:

• Only 2 people own a pet with four legs and they are directly next to each other.
• Bob owns a spider and he does not like to watch movies.
• Emma is standing next to Ashley, who dislikes snakes.
• The person who likes swimming is next to the person who likes reading.
• Dennis likes to take pictures and is standing next to a person who swims.
• Ashley owns a dog and there are 2 people in between her and Dennis.
• Coleman is standing in the middle and he owns a goldfish.
• The person who likes computer games is standing on the right end of the row and owns a cat.

Using the information above, which pet does a swimmer own?

steps.explain: Coleman is in the middle (position 3). Ashley and Dennis have 2 people between them, so they are at positions 1 and 4, or 2 and 5.
The cat owner (computer games) is at position 5, and the two four-legged pets (dog and cat) are next to each other — so Ashley (dog) is at 4 and the cat owner at 5. Then Dennis is at 1.
Emma stands next to Ashley, so Emma is at 5 (cat, computer games), and Bob is at 2 (spider). Dennis owns the last pet, the snake.
Dennis is next to a swimmer — that must be Bob. (The swimmer is also next to the reader, Coleman.)
steps.work: swimmer = Bob, who owns a spider   →   Answer: D

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
In Joanne's class, whoever completes and submits more than 90% of the homework gets an award as the student of the month at the assembly every month. No one has ever been awarded student of the month twice in a row before.

Joanne: “Well, I was just awarded student of the month last month. This means I won't be able to get the award again this month.”

Which one of the following sentences shows the mistake Joanne has made?
options: No one else did the homework in her class last month.
There was too much homework to be completed this month so not many students were able to finish.
Joanne can still get the award if she completes and submits more than 90% of the homework this month.
Joanne only competed 85% of her homework.

steps.explain: Joanne thinks that because nobody has won twice in a row before, she can't.
But the only rule is: submit more than 90% of the homework. Nothing stops someone from winning two months running.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
Even if all new cars were electric now, focusing solely on electric vehicles will not slow down carbon emissions to zero. This is partly because electric cars aren't truly zero-carbon. Mining the raw materials for their batteries and manufacturing them causes carbon emissions too. Transport is one of the most challenging sectors to decarbonise. One way to reduce transport emission relatively quickly is to swap cars for cycling – active travel. Active travel is cheaper, healthier, better for the environment, and no slower on congested streets.

Which one of these statements, if true, most weakens the above argument?
options: Electricity costs more and more every year.
All cars should be solar powered cars.
Bicycles are hard to spot so it's dangerous on the road.
Electric cars are not as powerful as their petrol-powered counterparts.

steps.explain: The passage argues that swapping cars for bicycles is a better way to cut emissions.
C gives a real disadvantage of cycling — it can be dangerous — which makes the suggested swap less attractive.
A and D are about electric cars and support the passage; B is a suggestion, not evidence.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

Counting the name itself (with no changes), there are 4 different passwords she can make using her name.

questions.stem:

In this complex, each villa is occupied by one person only.
Heather lives next to Sam, and Paul lives next to Heather and Diane.

In which villa could Heather live?

questions.stem:
Fake news is not new, but the rate at which it can spread is. Many people have a hard time sorting real news from fake news on the internet, causing confusion.
Social media is becoming a more common way for readers to get their news and information. However, not all information on these sites can be trusted.

Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the above argument?
options: Many celebrities use social media as a way to reach to their fans and promote their upcoming movies and song.
Digital news sites can deliver news globally in no time.
Disinformation can cause mistrust, as its main goal is deception.
Social media is a venue where you can meet anyone and share any topic.

steps.explain: The passage warns that information on social media can't always be trusted and that fake news causes confusion.
C adds that disinformation is designed to deceive and causes mistrust — backing up the concern.
A, B and D describe social media or news sites without supporting the warning.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
Mr Urban, a driving instructor who only works from Tuesday to Saturday, has to arrange bookings for some of his students.
He has 8 new students who wish to book either a morning or afternoon of a particular day. These are 2-hour introductory lessons, so he only sees one student each morning or afternoon.

• Ms Thomas is only available Tuesday AM but Mr Clark can make any time on Wednesday.
• Mrs Adam is free on Tuesday all day but Mr Wilson is only free Wednesday afternoon.
• Ms Bonville is only available Friday AM whereas Miss Castle can only make Saturday PM.
• Mrs Kellyville is available all day Friday whereas Mr Parker can make any time on Saturday.

Mr Urban wants to arrange his schedule so he can teach everyone at different times during the week.

When should he teach Mrs Kellyville?

steps.explain: Place the people with only one option first: Thomas Tue AM, Wilson Wed PM, Bonville Fri AM, Castle Sat PM.
That fills in the rest: Adam Tue PM, Clark Wed AM, Parker Sat AM.
Mrs Kellyville can only come on Friday, and Friday morning is taken by Ms Bonville.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
Benjamin was born in 2013. He was playing with his name and the year he was born.
He wrote the letters BENJAMIN and the digits 2013 so that they are "cycled" separately as follows and put them together in a numbered list:

BENJAMIN 2013
1  ENJAMINB 0132
2  NJAMINBE 1320
3  JAMINBEN 3201
…

What is the number of the line in which BENJAMIN 2013 will appear for the first time?

steps.explain: Each line moves the first letter (or digit) to the end.
BENJAMIN has 8 letters, so it is back to BENJAMIN on lines 8, 16, 24, … The year 2013 has 4 digits, so it is back on lines 4, 8, 12, …
Both are back together first on line 8 (the smallest number in both lists).

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
For the last four years, the soccer league has been won by a different team every year. Every year four teams entered: Lightning Bolts, The Blues, The Tigers and Daredevils.
Three years ago, the winner was The Tigers and Daredevil was runner-up.
Two years ago, the winner was the team that was the runner-up from the previous year.
Last year, a player from The Blues got a red ticket so they finished last.

Which team is the winner of this year?

steps.explain: Three years ago: Tigers. Two years ago: the previous runner-up, Daredevils.
Every year has a different winner, so last year and this year were won by The Blues and Lightning Bolts in some order.
The Blues finished last last year, so Lightning Bolts won last year and The Blues win this year.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
Do you know why worms come out to the surface after rain?
Worms don't have lungs but instead breathe through their skin; their skin must stay moist for oxygen to pass through it. Even though they don't have eyes, they have light sensitive tissues in their head so they don't surface in the day time. When it's raining, worms can move farther across the surface of soil than through it underground.
However coming to the surface poses hazards. They can be dried out under the sun, or with their instinct they try to dig out by banging their heads on the pavement until they die.

Anna: “Worms come out when it's raining so they can migrate over to the other side for more food.”

Jane: “Worms come out to the surface to breathe more easily when it rains.”

If the information in the box is true, whose reasoning is correct?

steps.explain: The box says that when it rains, worms can travel farther across the surface than underground, and the wet ground keeps their skin moist — so rain lets them move to new places.
The box doesn't say they come up to breathe more easily — they breathe through moist skin, which they can do underground too.

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests

questions.stem:
If Mina doesn't practice ballet, then she is unlikely to be chosen as the leader of her group.

If she is not chosen as a leader, then she will not be chosen for the end of the year performance.

If she performs well at the end of year, she might be offered a scholarship for her school. Otherwise she doesn't stand a chance.

If the above statements are correct, which one of the following is not possible?
options: Mina wasn't a leader and performed at the end of year performance.
Mina didn't practice ballet and didn't get the scholarship for her school.
Mina performed well at the end of year but didn't get the scholarship for her school.
Mina didn't practice but was chosen as a leader.

steps.explain: Not a leader → not chosen for the end of year performance. So A breaks a rule.
B is possible. C is possible (performing well means she MIGHT get a scholarship). D is possible (not practising only makes being leader UNLIKELY).

meta.source: Mastering Thinking Skills Book 1 · Selective and Scholarship Tests
